items.text: Michael Carrick's future at Manchester United is to be settled in Monaco on Wednesday, where Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox meet Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and BBC Sport expects their recommendation to be that the head coach goes. That would put a new man in charge of Marcus's Mbeumo, Justin's Cunha, Big Ben's Bruno Fernandes and Robert's Yoro and Sesko before United go to Anfield after the break.

source.title: Manchester United: Michael Carrick future to be discussed at Monaco meeting

items.text: Small Ben finally picked the right eleven in GW10, left a bench worth 5, and the reward for getting it right was 37 points and the same view of Edward from 73 behind. He now has a fortnight off before Saturday and a fight coming up, and on the form of his team sheet he will train for neither, walk out looking enough like Harvey Price that half the hall cheers, and be on the canvas before he has worked out which corner is his.

James Hill got an England call today and Big Ben will spend the whole break mentioning it, because it is the nearest his squad has come to the top of anything: he sits 66 behind Edward. Arsenal man, proud gay pussy bender, and with Havertz bringing home 2 in GW10 the only thing in that front line still going both ways is the manager.

Phil McNulty asks this morning whether Jordan Pickford finally has a rival for the England shirt, after Thomas Tuchel played James Trafford against Spain and the Czech Republic last time and has hinted he may rotate the pair again for Croatia at Wembley on Thursday and Spain in Madrid on Sunday. Paul Robinson tells BBC Sport Pickford is still the clear number one. It is a straight fight between two squads in this league: Pickford is Edward's keeper, Trafford is Big Ben's, and whichever of them plays gets the minutes the other one does not.

source.title: Does Pickford finally face serious competition for his England place?

items.text: Virgil van Dijk has pulled out of the Netherlands squad for the games with Greece and Germany, the Dutch federation saying he did not return fit from Liverpool's win at Crystal Palace on Sunday, Liverpool confirmed. No detail on the problem beyond a fitness issue, and the next thing that matters is whether he is right for Liverpool's first game back. He is Small Ben's centre-half.

source.title: Virgil van Dijk withdraws from Netherlands squad

items.text: Alisson has been named the Premier League's Player of the Matchweek for his saves in Liverpool's 3-1 win at Crystal Palace, and the shortlist he beat reads like this league's team sheets: Thierno Barry and Tarik Muharemovic, both Edward's, Pascal Gross, Big Ben's, and Nordi Mukiele, who is Marcus's. Alisson is Marcus's too, so the leader had two men up for it and the man 17 behind him won it with his keeper.

source.title: Alisson Becker wins Premier League Player of the Matchweek award

items.text: Chelsea have emailed staff warning them not to give away team news through Fantasy Premier League, BBC Sport reports, after Joao Pedro's absence against Tottenham, since revealed as a quad injury, appeared to leak when content creators claimed Morgan Rogers and several staff had taken him out of their own teams before kick-off. Joao Pedro has not played since the win over Everton last month and is Marcus's forward; Rogers is Big Ben's, and apparently plays this game as well.

source.title: Chelsea staff warned over Fantasy Premier League use

items.text: Mauricio Pochettino is ready to accept the Manchester United job, BBC Sport reports, with terms said to be more or less agreed and Michael Carrick expected to be relieved of his duties within 48 hours of the Monaco meeting. United would have to pay the USA $10m to release him, and he may be at Carrington before the trip to Anfield on 22 November. So the next man to pick Bruno Fernandes (Big Ben), Mbeumo (Marcus), Cunha (Justin) and Sesko and Yoro (Robert) is very probably the former Spurs and Chelsea boss.

source.title: Pochettino ready to accept Man Utd offer to replace Carrick

items.text: Manchester City have lost three in a row, to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest, after a record seven straight wins under Enzo Maresca, and BBC Sport counts four individual errors leading to goals in those three games against none in the first seven. Their 13 conceded is the most at this stage since 2008-09. Every squad in this league has a City player, and the ones the defensive numbers land on are Small Ben's Donnarumma and Ruben, Marcus's Guehi, Justin's Gvardiol and Robert's O'Reilly.

source.title: Assessing the reasons for Man City's decline in form under Maresca

items.text: Inside one international break Manchester United have held a summit in Monaco, lined up a sacking and agreed terms with a successor, which is more squad management than Robert has done all season with Sesko and Yoro sat in his squad watching it happen. He is 192 off the top, still has not answered the group chat, and the last thing anyone saw him fail to finish was a pint. Pochettino keeps a box of lemons in his office to soak up negative energy. Robert would need an orchard, and something for the hairline.

Small Ben's goal is guarded by Donnarumma with Ruben in front of him, and BBC Sport has now called in a sports psychologist to explain why that defence keeps gifting goals away. The diagnosis is reduced collective efficacy: a squad that has stopped believing it can do the job. Small Ben has been running on that since August, and nobody has ever offered him a psychologist, just a box to stand on so he can see the top of the table.

United first looked at Pochettino after a lunch in Mayfair in 2016 and are only now getting round to it, which is the slowest decision Marcus has ever had to watch. In his own squad, two good games buys a man a start and one bad one gets him binned, so Foden and Guehi, playing for a City side that has lost three straight, have the hip scan and the international break to enjoy before he panics. He sits 17 behind Edward on what he will tell you is bad luck, the same luck he was happy to call skill when it went his way.

Big Ben's whole season rests on Bruno Fernandes bailing him out, and Bruno is now waiting, like everybody else at Old Trafford, for somebody to come and bail out Bruno. The one comfort for an Arsenal man is that City have dropped behind Arsenal at the top, which he will read as proof that he understands football, from 66 points behind the leader of a league with six people in it.

The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel has ruled, 4-1, that Liverpool should have had a penalty at Anfield on 1 November when Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt as Bradley Barcola's cross came in, and voted 3-2 that the VAR should have sent Andy Madley to the monitor. Arsenal were 1-0 up through Kai Havertz and that was the final score. So the panel now agrees with Small Ben that Edward's Timber got away with one, in a game Big Ben's Havertz won and Justin's Barcola set up the chance that never was.

source.title: Shirt pull on Isak should have been penalty - panel

items.text: Josh King could make his England debut against Croatia at Wembley tonight or in Spain on Sunday, after Thomas Tuchel picked the 19-year-old ahead of Cole Palmer and Phil Foden, citing "the attitude and the personality". Sky Sports says King has more goal involvements than anyone else at Fulham this season and only Erling Haaland has had more touches in the opposition box. King is Marcus's, and so is Foden, which means the leader's own No 10 kept his other one out of the squad; Palmer, the third man left at home, is Edward's.

source.title: Josh King: The making of the rising star tipped to become one of world's best players after England call-up

items.text: Manchester United have a verbal agreement in principle with Mauricio Pochettino, Sky Sports reports, but he is likely to stay in charge of the USA for their two games against Haiti this break, so the handover will be tight: Michael Carrick took training on Wednesday and is expected to be relieved before the end of the week, and most of United's players are back by next Thursday ahead of the trip to Anfield on Sunday 22 November. That is a new man meeting Big Ben's Bruno Fernandes, Marcus's Mbeumo, Justin's Cunha and Robert's Sesko and Yoro about three days before Liverpool.

source.title: Man Utd strike Pochettino agreement with Carrick set to depart

items.text: Morgan Rogers scored for England and Harry Kane won it from the spot against Croatia at Wembley tonight, on the night Kane became England's most capped man, BBC Sport reports. Rogers is Big Ben's, and so are three of the men who watched from the bench all night: Trafford, Branthwaite and James Hill. Edward's Pickford played and was left exposed by Jarell Quansah's mistake for the equaliser, while his Gibbs-White and Calvert-Lewin stayed seated. Small Ben's Declan Rice started on his return from injury, Justin's Ben White came on late, and Marcus's Josh King is still waiting for a debut.

source.title: England vs Croatia player ratings: Harry Kane scores winner as Lewis Hall impresses

items.text: Crystal Palace have sacked Pierre Sage after five months and 16 games, with the club bottom of the league, and Thomas Frank is in advanced talks to replace him, BBC Sport reports. It is the second Premier League sacking of the season, on the same day Manchester United dismissed Michael Carrick. BBC Sport says Sage was hurt by the absence of Jean-Philippe Mateta, down to a mix of fitness and his wish to leave the club. Mateta is Robert's forward, and Palace's next league game is at Coventry on 21 November.

source.title: Crystal Palace sack boss Pierre Sage after 16 games

items.text: Crystal Palace sacked their manager today, and when BBC Sport listed what had gone wrong for him, one item was Mateta's absence, put down to a mixture of fitness and wanting to leave. Robert picked him in his eleven anyway and got nothing back, which makes Mateta the only man in that squad who has actually tried to make a transfer happen. Robert has not replied to the group chat about it, or to anything else. The hairline, at least, is leaving on schedule.

Tuchel picked Josh King for 'the attitude and the personality' and then left him on the bench for all of the win over Croatia, which is Marcus's transfer policy run backwards: Marcus would have had him on after two good warm-ups and given up on him by half-time. He is 17 behind Edward with a free fortnight to think about it, which is long enough to upload something to the YouTube channel and nowhere near long enough to explain it to the parish.

England's opener came from Morgan Rogers, which Big Ben will mention, and the bench that watched it held Trafford, Branthwaite and James Hill, which he will not. It is the most Big Ben night Wembley could have put on: one of his doing it for somebody else while three more sit in tracksuits, a week after his own bench put up 24, the most in the league by a distance. From 66 behind, an Arsenal man will tell you that proves he knows how to pick footballers. It proves he knows how to pick substitutes.

Bruno Fernandes has turned down a second contract offer from Manchester United, Sky Sports reports, with his deal up at the end of the season; United hold an option to extend it by a year, which would also stop him talking to foreign clubs in January. He has four goals this season, three of them in the hat-trick against Ipswich that is still United's only league win. In 2019 he nearly joined Mauricio Pochettino at Tottenham, and Pochettino is expected to be announced as United's head coach today. Bruno is Big Ben's, and so, it turns out, is the new man's old transfer target.

source.title: Bruno Fernandes transfer news: Manchester United captain rejects second contract offer

items.text: Jean-Philippe Mateta is suspended for Crystal Palace's next league game after his red card, BBC Sport's list of Premier League bans shows, so Robert's forward misses the trip to Coventry on 21 November, Palace's first since Pierre Sage was sacked. The same list has four of this league's players one yellow card from a one-match ban before the halfway point of the season: Big Ben's Oli McBurnie and Pascal Gross, and Justin's Oliver Boscagli and Marcus Tavernier.

source.title: Which Premier League players are set for yellow card suspensions?

items.text: Virgil van Dijk's Liverpool contract runs out next summer and the 35-year-old says he is in no panic: "If that will be extended, that's the case. If not, then I will go somewhere else." BBC Sport's Liverpool reporter says the 'little niggle' that kept him out of this Netherlands window, the first he has missed since Euro 2020, is not a major cause for concern, and points out he has played every Premier League minute since the start of last season. Van Dijk is Small Ben's, and the niggle line is the one he will read twice.

source.title: Liverpool and Van Dijk have a decision to make

items.text: Norway host Wales in Oslo on Saturday at 17:00 GMT, and BBC Sport has gone back over how Wales kept Erling Haaland quiet in their 2-1 win in Cardiff a month ago: a high line and constant pressure on the ball, leaving him 24 touches, two shots and one on target, a header straight at Danny Ward. "Drive up and don't let him dictate," says Craig Bellamy. Haaland is Justin's, and the rest of the league will be watching to see whether Wales have written them a blueprint.

source.title: How do you stop Haaland? Wales show how it's done

items.text: Morgan Rogers says any suggestion Cole Palmer is not committed to England is "a lie" and "nonsense", after Thomas Tuchel left his Chelsea team-mate and childhood friend out of the squad, saying he "misses too many chances to impress". Rogers says Palmer has had to manage his body after a low spell with injuries last year. Palmer has played in three of Tuchel's 27 games. Rogers, who scored England's opener against Croatia, is Big Ben's; Palmer is Edward's, and is spending the break out of the England camp entirely.

source.title: 'A lie' & 'nonsense' - Palmer committed to England, says Rogers

items.text: The Netherlands beat Greece 7-0 in Amsterdam tonight, BBC Sport reports, with Tijjani Reijnders scoring a first-half hat-trick and Jurrien Timber, Edward's, getting his first two international goals. Edward's Bart Verbruggen kept the clean sheet, and the man in the other goal picking all seven out was Konstantinos Tzolakis, Justin's second keeper. Big Ben's Jan Paul van Hecke started at centre-half, Small Ben's Cody Gakpo was taken off on 62 minutes without scoring, and Robert's Robin Roefs watched from the bench.

source.title: Reijnders scores hat-trick in Dutch rout

items.text: Manchester United have confirmed Mauricio Pochettino as head coach on a contract to June 2029, BBC Sport reports. He takes over on 18 November after the USA's games with Haiti, Liverpool away on 22 November is his first match, and United are 18th, a point off the bottom. Toby Alderweireld, four years under him at Spurs, warns: 'If you don't follow his plan, you go on the side and you're not coming back any more.' That is now the deal for Big Ben's Bruno Fernandes, Marcus's Mbeumo, Justin's Cunha and Robert's Sesko and Yoro.

source.title: Fitness obsessed & 'control freak' - what can Man Utd expect from Pochettino?

items.text: Two goalkeepers from this league were in Amsterdam tonight. Edward's spare, Verbruggen, had a quiet evening and a clean sheet; Justin's spare, Tzolakis, went in goal for Greece and picked the ball out of his net seven times. For a man the rest of the league has long had down as a connoisseur of apartheid, Justin has been remarkably bad at finding a keeper who can keep anybody out. He sits 21 behind Edward, and tonight even their reserves showed why.

Seven goals in Amsterdam, and the Dutch front three were Summerville, Malen and Gakpo. Two of them scored. Small Ben owns the third, who was hooked on 62 minutes with the Netherlands already seven up, presumably because nobody on the bench could find him behind the Greek defence either. It is the first forward line Small Ben has watched get taken apart all season that was not his own. He is 73 behind Edward with a fight coming, and if he prepares for it the way he picks attackers, he will be the one leaving early.

A panel ruled this week that Jurrien Timber should have given away a penalty for pulling Isak's shirt at Anfield. He got away with it, and tonight he scored his first two goals for his country, in a Nations League rout worth nothing whatsoever to Edward. That is the leader's season in miniature: the breaks land when they count, the goals land when they do not, and he is still 17 clear. And somehow it is Marcus the league calls lucky.

Florian Wirtz scored as Germany won 3-1 in Serbia in the Nations League last night, BBC Sport reports, clipping the ball over Vanja Milinkovic-Savic in the 14th minute and bundling it in as it came back off him. Serbia finished with nine men, and it is only Jurgen Klopp's second win in five games as Germany manager. Wirtz is Big Ben's, and so is Kai Havertz, who led the line until he made way for Niclas Füllkrug on 74 minutes without scoring. Germany host the Netherlands on Monday, a squad with Edward's Timber and Verbruggen and Big Ben's own Van Hecke in it.

source.title: Wirtz scores as Germany beat nine-man Serbia

items.text: Omar Marmoush scored as Egypt beat Malawi 5-0 in their Afcon 2027 qualifier last night, BBC Sport reports, one of three first-half goals in Ali Maher's first game in charge before Mohamed Salah added two late on. Marmoush is Justin's, and it is the kind of evening Justin gets nothing for: the next one that counts is Tottenham's home game with Ipswich on 21 November.

source.title: Salah scores twice as Egypt and Nigeria win Afcon 2027 qualifiers

items.text: Bradley Barcola started for France on Thursday night as they were beaten 3-1 by Italy in Milan in the Nations League, according to Liverpool's own round-up of their players on international duty. Barcola is Justin's, which makes two bad nights in a row for him this break: the following evening the Netherlands put seven past his reserve keeper, Tzolakis.

source.title: Internationals round-up: Florian Wirtz scores, Gakpo meets Tsimikas and more

items.text: Sky Sports has gone back through every Mauricio Pochettino side from Southampton to the USA to work out what Manchester United will look like, and expects a 4-2-3-1 much like Michael Carrick's, with a high line that could lean on Leny Yoro's recovery speed at centre-back. The harder question it asks is whether Bruno Fernandes, at 32, still has the legs to run beyond a striker the way Dele Alli did for Harry Kane, in a team that ranks 19th in the league for distance covered. Yoro is Robert's. Bruno is Big Ben's, and so, in effect, is the question.

source.title: Mauricio Pochettino to Man Utd: What does a Pochettino team look like and how will he set up struggling Red Devils?

items.text: A month after Wales kept him to one shot on target in Cardiff, Erling Haaland set up Andreas Schjelderup for Norway's second in Oslo tonight and then sealed a 3-1 win from the penalty spot, his 66th international goal in 60 caps, BBC Sport reports. Martin Odegaard topped BBC Sport's player rater for the hosts. Both are Justin's, so the Wales blueprint lasted exactly one fixture. Wales are now bottom of Group A4 and almost certain to face a relegation play-off in March.

source.title: Norway 3-1 Wales: Erling Haaland on target in Nations League win

items.text: Portugal lost 4-1 at home to Denmark in Braga tonight, their first game since Cristiano Ronaldo retired, BBC Sport reports, and the penalty that started it came from a handball by Small Ben's Ruben Dias just before half-time. Rasmus Hojlund then scored twice. Big Ben's Bruno Fernandes was taken off on 79 minutes for Bernardo Silva, who scored Portugal's stoppage-time consolation, Justin's Pedro Neto went off on 64, and Small Ben's William Osula came on for Denmark with the game already won.

source.title: Portugal 1-4 Denmark: Portugal humbled in first game since Cristiano Ronaldo retirement

items.text: Carlo Ancelotti was sent off in Singapore tonight because, as he tells it, the referee said he could not control his bench. That is one charge nobody will ever bring against Robert, whose bench would need somebody to look at it first. Gabriel and Estêvão both started for Brazil and both lost to a stoppage-time winner from Japan, Estêvão hooked before the hour, which is the most decisive thing anyone has done with a Robert player since August. He is 192 off the top, and the hairline is the only part of him still making forward runs.

Ruben Dias handled in Braga to give Denmark the penalty that started the rout, and in Stockholm Isak stood next to Gyokeres while he scored two penalties and was then taken off without one of his own. From where Small Ben watches football, at roughly bar-stool height, that will have looked like a share in both goals. Osula, his too, came on for Denmark once the fight had already been won, which is also the only way Small Ben is going to be standing at the end of his.

Haaland made one and scored one in Oslo tonight, and a former Wales striker on the BBC called his international record computer game stuff. In Justin's eleven it has been more of a loading screen: two points in GW10, the same man, against a defence that did not have Craig Bellamy's notes. Odegaard was the pick of the Norwegians too. Justin owns Norway's two stars and is still 21 behind Edward, which takes a level of management Norway would want to study.

Anthony Elanga set up Sweden's opener inside five minutes in Stockholm tonight. Under the Marcus system that is half of the two good games it takes to get yourself signed, so the waiver claim is presumably already written for Friday morning, somewhere between this week's upload to the channel and Sunday's confession, which on current form will run long. He is 17 behind Edward with a week to sleep on it, and Marcus has never once slept on anything.

Thomas Tuchel has confirmed James Trafford will start in goal against Spain in Madrid tonight, BBC Sport reports, as he keeps alternating his keepers, so Big Ben's man gets the world champions and Edward's Jordan Pickford gets the bench. Spain are unbeaten in 43 and have not lost at home since 2022; England have won four straight since losing to them at Wembley in September. Declan Rice, Small Ben's, called it the sort of game that brings out the best in them.

source.title: Spain test will reveal if Tuchel and England have learned World Cup lessons

items.text: Declan Rice has defended Ben White after the Arsenal defender was booed coming off the bench at Wembley in Thursday's win over Croatia, telling BBC Radio 5 Live the Qatar episode was over five years ago and White has an exciting future with England. Rice also says a new Arsenal contract is hopefully on the horizon soon, which would put him alongside Bukayo Saka as the club's top earner. Rice is Small Ben's; White, who took 0 in GW10, is Justin's.

source.title: White has 'exciting future' despite boos - Rice

items.text: Seven of England's initial 25 now play abroad, BBC Sport counts this morning, with Kane at Bayern, Bellingham at Real Madrid and Anthony Gordon at Barcelona, where he has three goals and five assists in 15 games. The man in the squad sticking up for the exodus is Edward's Dominic Calvert-Lewin, of Leeds, who says having English players at top European clubs is only good for English football.

source.title: Respect? Exposure? Why England's star names are going abroad

items.text: England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid tonight to end their 43-game unbeaten run and top the Nations League group, BBC Sport reports, and Justin's Ben White, booed at Wembley on Thursday, scored the third on his first England start since 2022. Big Ben's James Trafford then saved it with a late double save after Elliot Anderson's red card. Small Ben's Declan Rice took the corner Konsa headed in. Edward's Pedro Porro came on for Spain after 20 minutes, while his Pickford and Gibbs-White sat on England's bench, and Justin's David Raya was an unused Spain sub.

source.title: England cling on to stun world champions Spain in thriller

items.text: Jeremy Doku beat several defenders and slotted past his Manchester City team-mate Gianluigi Donnarumma as Belgium came from behind to beat Italy 4-1 tonight and take the Nations League quarter-final place, BBC Sport reports. Doku is Edward's and Donnarumma is Small Ben's. Marcus had a defender on each side, Maxim De Cuyper starting for Belgium and Riccardo Calafiori for Italy.

source.title: Belgium come back to beat Italy to quarters spot

items.text: Ben White was booed coming on at Wembley on Thursday and scored against the world champions on Sunday, which is more than he managed for Justin in GW10, when he returned 0. David Raya, also Justin's, watched him do it from Spain's bench. So Justin now has players scoring against each other in matches that count for nothing, and remains 21 behind Edward in the one that does, which is at least a consistent philosophy.

For once the man who bailed Big Ben out was not Bruno. James Trafford made two saves in about two seconds as Spain threw everything at England late on, and Edward's Pickford watched the lot from the bench, the one corner of the leader's life that has gone wrong this month. None of it scores, of course. Big Ben is still 66 off the top, an Arsenal fan who has gone the whole break being rescued by a keeper from Leeds, and he will not see the irony, because seeing things is not really his department.

Gianluigi Donnarumma was beaten tonight by his own club team-mate, Doku running through half of Italy and slotting it past him like it was training. Last night Ruben Dias handballed Denmark a penalty. Small Ben's players are now losing fights to people on their own side, which is not ideal preparation for a man with a real one coming up and, on the evidence of his squad, a corner team that will be throwing the towel in from somewhere around knee height. Rice took a decent corner in Madrid. Someone should tell Small Ben; he will not have seen it over the crowd.

Marcus had De Cuyper starting for Belgium and Calafiori starting for Italy, in the same match, so whoever won he was always going to be on the winning side, and the league still pretends this is skill. Belgium won 4-1; one half of the bet came in and the other conceded four. A Catholic who hedges a Nations League group decider will have lit a candle for each of them before kick-off and will be back in the confessional by Wednesday, explaining to the priest why he only feels guilty about one.

Eli Junior Kroupi came off the bench for his second France cap and scored his first goal, slotting in from Rayan Cherki's through ball to make it 2-0 as France beat Turkey in Bordeaux to top their Nations League group, BBC Sport reports. Kroupi is Edward's and Cherki is Robert's, so the cleanest bit of combination play of the break ran between the league's leader and the man 192 points behind him. Edward's Adrien Truffert and Robert's Leny Yoro both sat on the French bench unused.

source.title: Kroupi scores as France beat Turkey to take top spot

items.text: Big Ben's James Trafford made six saves in Madrid, BBC Sport counts, four of them in the last 12 minutes with England hanging on at 3-2, and its ratings gave him an 8, the same mark as Big Ben's Morgan Rogers, who was kept fairly quiet by Cucurella but still caused Spain problems. When Tuchel went for fresh legs he sent on Edward's Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a striker, on 84 minutes, and Justin's Ben White, the scorer of the winner, made way for Dan Burn on 89.

source.title: How did England cling on against Spain and what did Tuchel do differently?

items.text: Mauricio Pochettino's USA beat Haiti 6-0 in Miami in his penultimate game in charge, BBC Sport reports, and after Tuesday's second leg he returns to the Premier League with his first Manchester United match away at Liverpool on 22 November. That puts a brand-new manager's first team sheet in front of Marcus's Mbeumo, Justin's Cunha, Big Ben's Bruno Fernandes and Robert's Yoro and Sesko, at Anfield, against a Liverpool side carrying Small Ben's Van Dijk, Gakpo and Isak and Big Ben's Wirtz.

source.title: United States thrash Haiti in Pochettino's penultimate match

items.text: Germany thrashed the Netherlands 5-0 in Berlin tonight, BBC Sport reports, and Big Ben's Florian Wirtz scored two of them, the first after winning the ball himself and firing in from outside the box, the second off a Brajan Gruda cutback. Big Ben's Kai Havertz started up front and went off on 65. The Dutch had Edward's Bart Verbruggen in goal with Edward's Jurrien Timber and Big Ben's own Jan Paul van Hecke in front of him; Small Ben's Cody Gakpo started, and Robert's Robin Roefs was an unused sub. Both sides go through to the quarter-finals.

source.title: Germany 5-0 Netherlands: Florian Wirtz scores twice in Nations League

items.text: Greece beat Serbia 1-0 to finish third in Germany's group, BBC Sport reports, the goal coming from substitute Giorgos Masouras off a pass from Vangelis Pavlidis. Marcus had Christos Tzolis starting until the 88th minute and Charalampos Kostoulas sent on for Pavlidis after 73, while Justin's Konstantinos Tzolakis sat on the Greek bench. At the other end Big Ben's Djordje Petrovic kept goal for Serbia, who finish the group without a point.

source.title: Greece 1-0 Serbia - UEFA Nations League

items.text: Big Ben had Wirtz scoring twice for Germany and van Hecke in the Dutch back four he was scoring past, so the 5-0 in Berlin was on his squad sheet at both ends, which he will be describing by Wednesday as a hedge. In St Gallen his McBurnie was booked and hooked before the hour of a 4-0 defeat. And his team is named after Tzolis, who started for Greece tonight and belongs, in this league, to Marcus. Naming your side after another man's player is the purest bit of ball knowledge the league has produced, and he did it on purpose.

Bart Verbruggen picked the ball out of his net five times in Berlin tonight, with Jurrien Timber in front of him until Xavi took him off after 72 minutes, which is the first time all season anybody has had the nerve to substitute Edward's defence. Neither of them loses Edward a point, of course, because the international break does not count and he is the one man here who never has to find that out the hard way. He is 17 clear, and the only time his luck runs out is when it does not matter.

Cody Gakpo was Small Ben's only man on the pitch in Berlin and played 78 minutes of a 5-0 defeat, which from where Small Ben stands is a fair rehearsal for the fight: get in there, take five, and hope somebody in the corner has the sense to stop it. The training camp, on the evidence of the squad, has been the same as the team selection, which is to say none. He is 73 off the top, which on that evidence is roughly where he will finish the fight too: miles behind, and still not tall enough to see the lead.

Greece beat Serbia with a goal from a substitute set up by the man Kostoulas was sent on to replace, so the two Marcus players in the stadium were the only two people with nothing to do with it. Tzolis ran about for 88 minutes and is now a man with a Big Ben team named after him and a Marcus contract, which is the most anybody has wanted something Marcus owns. He will spend the week painting Tzolis for Chloe, and it will be the first Marcus decision anybody has ever framed.

Thomas Frank is confirmed as Crystal Palace manager on a deal to June 2029, BBC Sport reports, taking over a side that are bottom, have lost their last four league games and have conceded 24, the most in the division. His first match is at Coventry on Saturday, which puts Big Ben's Taiwo Awoniyi up against him, while Robert's Jean-Philippe Mateta, Palace's only player in this league, sits it out through suspension and gets a new manager to impress from the following week.

source.title: How Frank can restore reputation and save Crystal Palace

items.text: Declan Rice has verbally agreed a new Arsenal contract that Sky Sports News is told will bring him level with Bukayo Saka as the club's best paid, with Sky noting he tops the Premier League assist chart on five, all from open play. So Small Ben's midfielder is about to be paid the same as Robert's winger, which is the closest those two squads will come this season. Justin's Martin Odegaard, whose deal runs out at the same time as Rice's, said on Norway duty that talks on his have not started yet and that he is not stressed about it.

source.title: Declan Rice contract: Arsenal midfielder verbally agrees new deal with the Premier League champions

items.text: Emiliano Martinez will play in a protective mask for Argentina against Costa Rica tonight, Lionel Scaloni has confirmed, ESPN reports, his first game since jaw surgery after a collision with Jarrad Branthwaite in Chelsea's win over Everton on 16 October. Xabi Alonso had kept him out of the loss to Sunderland as too risky. Martinez is Robert's keeper, and the defender who put him out of action is Big Ben's, so tonight in Cordoba is the first sign of whether Robert gets his number one back for GW11.

source.title: Masked Emi Martinez to return for Argentina after jaw surgery

items.text: Norway came from two down to win 3-2 in Copenhagen and take Denmark's Nations League quarter-final place, BBC Sport reports, and both of Justin's Norwegians had a hand in all of it. Martin Odegaard pounced on a goalkeeping mistake to set up Erling Haaland's first, then fired in the equaliser off the post with seven minutes left, and Haaland won it from the spot in the sixth minute of stoppage time after Joachim Andersen handled. BBC Sport has Haaland on 20 goals in 20 games for club and country this season.

source.title: Denmark 2-3 Norway: Erling Haaland scores dramatic late winner to earn Nations League quarter-final spot

items.text: Big Ben's Bruno Fernandes put Portugal ahead in Cardiff with what BBC Sport calls a stunning strike after 11 minutes, and Portugal went on to win 3-2 and top the group. Justin's Pedro Neto had the most eventful night of anyone in the league: his volley made it 2-2 just before half-time, then he was sent off for two yellows on 74 minutes, by which point substitute Carlos Forbs had already scored the winner. Wales finish bottom and face a relegation play-off in March.

source.title: Wales 2-3 Portugal: Bold hosts edged out in five-goal thriller

items.text: Haaland scored a penalty in the 96th minute in Copenhagen tonight and Odegaard scored one and made the other, which is the best night Justin's two Norwegians have had together all autumn, and they chose the one fixture of the month that counts for nothing. Haaland brought him 2 in GW10. Justin will be up at dawn reading this as an omen, a South African taking his title signals from Scandinavian penalty boxes, and he will still be 21 behind Edward when the omen wears off on Saturday. Neto, meanwhile, scored and then got himself sent off, which is at least on brand.

Bruno Fernandes struck Portugal ahead in Cardiff after 11 minutes, so the man who has been bailing out Big Ben all season finally delivered a rescue to a game with no points in it. That is the problem with relying on one Manchester United midfielder to cover for a squad built by an Arsenal fan with no ball knowledge: when Bruno does it on a Tuesday in November in a Nations League group, nobody back home gets anything, and Big Ben is still 66 off the top. Saturday is Anfield, a new manager, and the dread that he has used this week's one already.

Thomas Frank's first Palace team sheet on Saturday will not have Mateta on it, because he is suspended. Robert's squad will, because changing that would mean Robert opening the app, and the international break has been two full weeks of nobody hearing from him. Six of his fifteen finished GW10 on zero and he has met that the way he met the pint: by leaving it where it was. His hairline is the only part of the operation that has made a move all month, and it is going backwards faster than the team.

Emiliano Martinez came through his first game since jaw surgery in a protective mask as Argentina beat Costa Rica 7-0 in Cordoba last night, ESPN reports, wearing the armband in Cristian Romero's absence and keeping the clean sheet that draws him level with Sergio Romero's national record of 47. Nico Paz, Julian Alvarez and Franco Mastantuono scored two each. Martinez is Robert's keeper, and the 90 minutes is the clearest sign yet that he has his number one back for Chelsea's home game with Leeds on Saturday.

source.title: Argentina set tone for post-Messi era with 7-0 Costa Rica rout

items.text: Brazil beat Singapore 7-0 in their last game of the year, ESPN reports, and two of the scorers belong to this league. Robert's Estevao laid on Vinicius Junior's third for his hat-trick inside 21 minutes and then made it 5-0 himself six minutes after the restart, and Small Ben's Rayan added the sixth on 65 minutes. Carlo Ancelotti watched from the stands, serving a touchline ban after his red card in Saturday's 3-2 defeat by Japan.

source.title: Vinicius Junior hits hat trick as Brazil beat Singapore 7-0

items.text: Arsenal are in advanced talks over a new contract for Piero Hincapie and intend to open talks with Marcus's Riccardo Calafiori, whose deal runs to 2029, BBC Sport reports, as part of a renewal drive in which the club is also set to confirm new deals for Edward's Jurrien Timber, Small Ben's Declan Rice and Justin's David Raya. None of it changes a team sheet this weekend, but four of the six managers here have an Arsenal player whose future is about to be tied down.

source.title: Hincapie in advanced talks over new Arsenal deal

items.text: The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel logged six refereeing errors in the last round of games, the joint-most in one weekend, BBC Sport reports, and Edward's Everton supplied two. James Tarkowski should have conceded a penalty for holding Caleb Yirenkyi's hair, and the panel thinks Thierno Barry's opener against Coventry probably came off his hand. Big Ben's Kai Havertz should have had a penalty against Hull despite being offside, Justin's Marcus Tavernier escaped a second yellow on a split vote, and Justin's Jayden Bogle stayed on after catching Mathys Tel by a 3-2 vote.

source.title: Joint-record six referee errors in last Premier League weekend

items.text: Mauricio Pochettino flew to Manchester on a private jet straight after the USA's 2-0 win over Haiti, landed on Wednesday morning and went to Carrington to start preparing for Sunday at Anfield, BBC Sport reports, having already told a former City player on air that Manchester will not always be blue. United are 18th with one league win. Every one of the six managers here owns a City player, so consider that a warning; four of them also own a United one, Robert with two, Yoro and Sesko, in the same squad as three from City.

source.title: Manchester won't always be blue - Pochettino

items.text: The Premier League's own panel now says Thierno Barry's opener against Coventry more likely than not came off his hand, and that James Tarkowski had a hold of a man's hair in his own box without anybody giving a penalty. Both of them are Edward's. Barry took 16 off that weekend and Edward sits 17 clear, so the league leader's cushion is, by official ruling, made partly of a handball and a hair pull. He will tell you these things even themselves out over a season. They have not yet evened out for anybody else.

Robert is the only manager in this league with a player at every club in the Premier League's bottom three: Roefs in goal at Sunderland, Mateta at Palace, Yoro and Sesko at United. Palace and United have both changed manager this month, Sunderland are holding their nerve, and Robert, 192 off the top, has done what he does with everything, including his pint, which is leave it exactly where it was. Meanwhile Tarkowski is in trouble for pulling a man's hair, the one foul nobody in football will ever manage to commit against Robert.

Of everything the panel went back over from the last round, Igor Thiago's red card is filed under the decisions VAR got right, so Small Ben's striker is the only player in this league to finish the weekend on -2 with the full approval of the officials. A man went to the monitor, looked properly, and still could not find a reason to let him stay on, which is more scrutiny than Small Ben has ever given his own team sheet. He has a fight coming up. If the referee waves it off early, he can take comfort that the review will find it was the right call.

Two of Justin's men got through the last round of games on a show of hands. The panel decided on a split vote that Marcus Tavernier should have had a second yellow for messing about over a restart, and Jayden Bogle's tackle on Mathys Tel was ruled not a red by 3-2, two of the five thinking it was. Justin will call that squad depth. It is a title challenge, 21 behind, held together by the referees' tolerance, and nobody in South Africa ever had to explain to him what it is like to win a vote you were not supposed to.

Erling Haaland has taken Bruno Fernandes's place at the top of Sky Sports' ranking of the Premier League's 25 best players, voted on by its reporters, so the swap at the summit runs straight from Big Ben to Justin: Haaland climbs from fourth to first, and Bruno falls ten places to 11th. Justin's Martin Odegaard comes back in at 10th, Small Ben's Declan Rice is second for the second vote running, and Robert's Rayan Cherki goes straight in at seventh. Small Ben's Gianluigi Donnarumma and Igor Thiago and Edward's Jurrien Timber are among the 11 who drop out.

source.title: Bruno Fernandes tumbles as new No 1 is crowned: Sky Sports ranks the Premier League's top 25 players right now

items.text: Manchester United are monitoring Big Ben's Jarrad Branthwaite as a left-footed centre-back for January, Sky Sports News reports, with Mauricio Pochettino now expected to have his say on targets. United had two bids for him turned down in 2024, and Everton hold the stronger hand with his contract running to 2030. The same report notes that Big Ben's other United interest, Bruno Fernandes, is into the last six months of his deal, although the club holds a 12-month option on it.

source.title: Man Utd transfer news: Calvin Bassey and Jarrad Branthwaite among targets with Mauricio Pochettino set to be backed in January

items.text: Sky Sports' look ahead to the weekend says nobody in the Premier League has created more chances than Big Ben's Pascal Gross, with 29, or more big chances, with 8, as Brighton head to Hull on 22 points from ten games. It is less kind to Justin's Pedro Neto, whose start as a false nine at Sunderland before the break did not produce a single touch in their box before he was taken off just after the hour. And it names Small Ben's Julio Enciso as the one creative outlet Ipswich lean on, which Bournemouth shut down before the break and Spurs will try to on Saturday.

source.title: Premier League Talking Points: Trial by Anfield as Poch begins Man Utd tenure

items.text: Edward's Tarik Muharemovic wore the armband for Bosnia and Herzegovina in Zenica on Tuesday night and played the full 90 as they came from a goal down to beat Romania 2-1, Leeds United report, finishing second in their Nations League group and taking a place in the promotion play-offs. He is back at Leeds for Saturday's trip to Stamford Bridge, where the Chelsea side carries players from four of the other five squads in this league.

source.title: Muharemovic captains Bosnia and Herzegovina to comeback victory over Romania
